Pandora has a mediocre, repetitive algorithm and is basically amateur hour. I have my own method!

I usually start with with an artist I like (I'll use Bob Dylan for the first example). I use sources like interviews, Wikipedia, and fan websites to answer these Qs:

1. Who are Bob Dylan's known influences? Hank Williams, Woody Guthrie, Paul Clayton, Little Richard

2. Who has he toured or collaborated with? Joan Baez, The Band

3. Who are some of his genre/era contemporaries? Cat Stevens, Nick Drake, Paul Simon

4. Who has he mentioned liking or admiring? Bono, Frank Sinatra

5. Who else have Bob's session personnel worked with? His longtime bassist, Tony Garnier, played with Robert Gordon, Tom Waits, and the nine-time Grammy winners Asleep at the Wheel

This works for more contemporary artists, too, like Amy Winehouse (and for different genres, like triphop and metal):

1. Who were some of Amy's influences? Billie Holiday, Tony Bennett, Dinah Washington

2. Who has she toured or collaborated with? Moby, MGMT, Paolo Nutini

3. Who are some of her genre/era contemporaries? Alanis Morissette, maybe Lady Gaga

4. Who has she mentioned liking or admiring? Before she died, Amy said in an interview that she was hoping to work with jazz groups Soweto Kinch, Jazz Jamaica and Tomorrow’s Warriors.

5. Who else have Amy's session personnel worked with? One of her producers, Gordon Williams, worked with Joss Stone, Damien Marley, and Carlos Santana on some very well-received albums

These two lists are quick examples that took me about 15 minutes, but this process can get way more get extensive if you want it to! From this point, I usually listen to one or two popular songs from each of the leads I write down on Spotify or YouTube. If I like what I hear, I listen to the whole album (if there are a lot of albums, I try to find out which one people seem to like the best, or maybe listen to the debut album). I really think an album is meant to be listened to as a complete work, not one song at a time, which is another thing that bugs me a little bit about Pandora.

In the end, this takes a lot less time and gives me a way more diverse list of new music than pretty much any other method I've tried.

That's actually why I never liked Pandora. I was always big on Last.fm when they were major competitors because they had a better algorithm. That's quite an interesting method you have there. I'm certain your music collection expands many genres.

Thank you! :) Last.fm was a bit better, but the way I see it, it's hard for any algorithm to really hone in on what it is that you like about a song or artist. This method came from my realizing that probably, a musician who "hangs out with" a musician I listen to is more likely to be up my alley than an artist who shares Pandora's "musical attributes."
